title.value: From Generative Models to Generative Passages: A Computational Approach to (Neuro) Phenomenology
title.justification: The full title of the paper is clearly stated in the beginning and throughout the text, highlighting the focus on a computational approach to phenomenology using generative models.
title.quote: This paper presents a version of neurophenomenology based on generative modelling techniques developed in computational neuroscience and biology.

extractions.description: The paper explores a computational approach to phenomenology using generative models, primarily in the context of naturalizing phenomenology through computational neuroscience techniques. It reviews philosophical objections, outlines the generative modelling framework, and discusses how it can be applied to model the inferential processes that explain lived experiences. The paper aims to integrate phenomenological descriptions with scientific methods to enhance understanding of consciousness.

primary_category.justification: The paper centralizes around the computational understanding of phenomenology and consciousness, a topic which does not explicitly fall within any eco-responsible category provided. Its focus is on bridging phenomenology and computational neuroscience rather than environmental or sustainability-related topics.
primary_category.quote: In summary, we describe a version of computational phenomenology which uses generative modelling to construct a computational model of the inferential or interpretive processes that best explain this or that kind of lived experience.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary eco-responsible themes apparent in the paper's focus on computational phenomenology and generative models, which are not aligned with environmental or sustainability objectives.
secondary_categories.quote: Our approach adopts a computational approach to the study of phenomenological experience, as it is understood and described by phenomenologists, and without making specific metaphysical assumptions about the metaphysics and mechanistic underpinnings of lived experience.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper’s content predominantly covers cognitive sciences and computational modelling approaches that do not align with the designated eco-responsible sub-categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: Essentially, our version of computational phenomenology is the form taken by generative modelling in cases where the data or observations that we want to explain by leveraging generative modelling is our first-person phenomenology itself.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The theme of the paper does not intersect with any secondary sub-categories related to eco-responsible AI, as it focuses chiefly on computational and philosophical aspects of consciousness.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The aim of this paper was to outline a conceptual and methodological framework for a particular approach to computational phenomenology.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper’s focus lies in using computational methods to understand phenomenology and consciousness, proposing a new scientific framework that doesn’t align with existing eco-responsible categories.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose a new approach to formal phenomenology based on generative modelling, under the rubric of ‘computational phenomenology’.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category reflects the paper’s specific interest in applying generative modelling techniques to study cognitive processes and consciousness—an area outside typical eco-responsible AI classifications.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our project is to revisit the program of neurophenomenology as the search for generative passages in light of recent developments in computational modelling (i.e., generative modelling, described below).
